newsitem.title: UK: Clarke-cabinet agrees Europe wait and see policy.
newsitem.headline: Clarke-cabinet agrees Europe wait and see policy.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday the full cabinet had agreed to stick to Britain's wait and see policy on a single European currency.
Clarke told reporters: "We were proceeding on the basis of the policy that we're going to negotiate and decide at the right time, and that was accepted by everybody."
A senior government source office confirmed that the cabinet had agreed the current "wait-and-see" policy.
But he said there was considerable scepticism in cabinet as to whether other European countries would comply strictly with the convergence criteria for entry into the single currency.
If this happened, the source said, "we think delay is better than (going ahead with) the current timetable".

But he said that if EMU went ahead without countries meeting the criteria necessary to make the single currency sustainable, then "we would not be a part of it... We would only join if the conditions are right and it is in Britain's national interest." -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7768
